newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Bank of Korea intervenes again in won/dlr trading.
newsitem.headline: Bank of Korea intervenes again in won/dlr trading.

text.p: The Bank of Korea offered to sell dollars in three-month forward trading at 905.50 won in what dealers said was its second such intervention in the interbank market in about 30 minutes.
The intervention was aimed at slowing the local currency's rapid drop against the U.S. unit, dealers said.
The central bank was earlier said to have offered to sell dollars at 916 won in six-month forward trading.
Bank of Korea officials were not immediately available for comment.
The won has been under pressure in connection with jitters over the financial troubles of the Kia Group, and in the aftermath of recent drops in the Thai and Philippine currencies.
Banks have offered protection for the eighth-ranked Kia Group, which was struggling under heavy debts.
